- RIGHT 2: ((39, 19), (39, 44)), completed=False
- RIGHT 3: ((39, 19), (39, 44)), completed=False

- RIGHT: left 14→19, right 44→39 → (39, 19), (39, 39)

- RIGHT 1: ((39, 14), (39, 44)), completed=False
- RIGHT 2: ((39, 19), (39, 44)), completed=False

RIGHT 2 from (39, 14), (39, 44) resulted in (39, 19), (39, 44). The left square moved from col 14 to 19, but the right square stayed at col 44. This is unexpected - the right square should have moved from col 44 to 39.
Hmm, maybe the right square hit a boundary at col 44 when at row 39. Let me check the ascii to see the black outline at row 39.
Actually, I think the issue is that the right square can't move left of col 44 when at row 39 because of the black outline boundary. The robot outline constrains the movement.
So the reachable horizontal positions depend on the row:
- Row 39: right square can only be at cols 44, 49 (can't go left of 44)
- Row 44: right square can be at cols 34, 39, 44, 49
- Row 49: right square can be at cols 34, 39, 44, 49

Let me re-examine the reachable configurations:
- Row 39: left col {9, 14, 19}, right col {44, 49} - but they're coupled, so:
  - (39, 9), (39, 49)
  - (39, 14), (39, 44)
  - (39, 19), (39, 44) - right can't move further left
- Row 44: left col {9, 14, 19, 24}, right col {34, 39, 44, 49}
- Row 49: left col {9, 14, 19, 24}, right col {34, 39, 44, 49}
So there are 3 + 4 + 4 = 11 reachable configurations (not 12).
I've visited:
- Row 39: (39, 9), (39, 49); (39, 14), (39, 44); (39, 19), (39, 44)
- Row 44: (44, 9), (44, 49); (44, 14), (44, 44); (44, 19), (44, 39); (44, 24), (44, 34)
- Row 49: (49, 9), (49, 49); (49, 14), (49, 44); (49, 19), (49, 39); (49, 24), (49, 34)
That's all 11 configurations, and none completed the level. So the goal is NOT about the blue square positions.
